Attached is a short RFP summary and our initial monthly usage estimate (very rough). Questions we have up front:
- Do you publish input/output split rates (we need those for our accounting)?
- Are there pilot discounts for a 3-month evaluation?
- Any per-model availability constraints (regional / capacity / dedicated pools)?

If easier, we are happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to walk through numbers.

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Hosted API baseline request: per-1M token IO split & supported models

Hi Emily — thanks for the note and the RFP. Welcome — excited to help.

Short answers up front: yes, we publish and quote per-1M token IO splits, and we have pilot discounts for evaluation pilots (details below). Attached is a short snapshot of our hosted baseline rates to get you started (Redwood_rate_snapshot.pdf).

A few clarifying Qs that will help me pick the right model set and tighten rates:
- Expected steady-state monthly token volume (the spreadsheet shows a wide range; can you confirm a target band?)
- Peak QPS (for latency planning) and percent of calls that produce >512 output tokens (affects model choice and caching)
- Any compliance constraints (PHI handling, region/state residency) — that can influence Dedicated vs Hosted recommendations

Example baseline per-1M IO rates (input / output) — hosted standard (no commit):
- redwood-alpha-1.4B: $4.00 (input) / $8.00 (output) per 1M tokens
- redwood-catalyst-7B: $9.00 (input) / $18.00 (output) per 1M tokens
- redwood-arc-13B: $18.00 (input) / $36.00 (output) per 1M tokens

Notes:
- Rates above are MSRP for hosted public API in the us region and reflect models with different memory/throughput profiles.
- Net effective price can change with pilot discounts, committed monthly spend, or multi-month contracts.
- We commonly recommend the 7B family for classification and high throughput; the 13B (arc) is typically chosen for higher-quality long-form generation where latency budget allows.
- We can enable prefix/KV caching which reduces output token costs when you repeatedly prompt similar contexts — happy to advise based on your workload.

Pilot discount: we can offer up to a 30% reduction on MSRP for the first 3 months on up to $X in spend with a light committed cadence (Aditya will propose exact bands).

Looping in Aditya (discounts/commit routing) and Ben (legal/contract). If you can share a preferred hour, we’ll set a short call and bring a one-page quote.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_rate_snapshot.pdf

Emily — quick follow from Olga. I pulled together a concise pilot quote so you have concrete numbers to evaluate. See the attached proposed_pilot_quote.pdf for full line items, but headline here:

Proposed pilot pricing (hosted API) — effective per-1M IO after pilot discount:
- redwood-alpha-1.4B: $3.00 (input) / $6.00 (output) per 1M tokens — 25% pilot discount
- redwood-catalyst-7B: $6.75 (input) / $13.50 (output) per 1M tokens — 25% pilot discount
- redwood-arc-13B: $13.50 (input) / $27.00 (output) per 1M tokens — 25% pilot discount

Commitment tiers (post-pilot pricing guidance):
- $0–5k/mo: standard MSRP above
- $5k–25k/mo: 10–20% off MSRP depending on term length
- >$25k/mo: 20–30% off MSRP with 12-month commitments (higher tiers available for Dedicated)

Availability notes: hosted model families are available in our primary us region; occupancy-based throttling can happen during rare capacity peaks — for production SLAs we often recommend Redwood Dedicated or reserved capacity.

One technical note we often get asked: KV / prefix cache reuse can significantly reduce billed output tokens when you reuse prompt context between calls — we’ll help optimize that in the POC.

If this looks good, can we lock a short call tomorrow (Wed 6/17) to align on volume bands and finalize the quote? Ben is on CC for contract redlines.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
